Report Description///POTENTIAL RELEASE REPORT/// ***CRITICAL INCIDENT COMMUNICATIONS (CIC) REPORT - INITIAL - CG AIRCRAFT CRASH - 22 JUN 202*** INCIDENT TYPE: COAST GUARD AIRCRAFT CRASH LOCATION: 3 MILES NORTH OF SITKA AIRPORT TIME INCIDENT OCCURRED: 1015 AKDT / 1815 ZULU TIME OF INITIAL REPORT TO NCC: 1430 / 1830 ZULU AMPLIFYING INFORMATION: • AT 1430 EDT ON JUNE 22, USCG AIR STATION SITKA REPORTED A COAST GUARD H60 CRASHED THREE MILES NORTH FROM THE SITKA AIRPORT IN MOUNTAIN TERRAIN. • A CALL WAS RECEIVED FROM ONE OF THE PILOTS. • ALL FOUR COAST GUARD MEMBERS ON BOARD ARE REPORTED ALIVE. • AIR STATION SITKA IS READY TO DEPLOY A SECOND AIRCRAFT FOR RESCUE MISSION. • LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT IS ENROUTE TO THE CRASH SITE WHICH IS ONE MILE FROM AN ACCESS ROAD. • US NATIONAL GUARD IS DEPLOYING A BLACK HAWK FOR SUPPORT. • THERE IS TFR SET IN PLACE IN THE AREA. • US COAST GUARD ARCTIC DISTRICT IS ASSUMING SAR MISSION COORDINATOR (SMC). • FOLLOWING CIC WILL BE AT 2030Z

THE RP STATES THIS WAS NEVER REPORTED TO ANY LOCAL, STATE, OR FEDERAL AGENCIES./// CALLER REPORTS A GAS STATION WAS FILLING ITS UNDERGROUND STORAGE TANKS WHEN HEAVY GAS FUMES BECAME APPARENT WITHIN THE STORE. THIS CAUSED IMMEDIATE HEALTH IMPACTS ON THE EMPLOYEES. UPON INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT GASOLINE WAS FLOWING OUT OF PIPING BEHIND THE STATION WHILE TANK FILLING WAS GOING ON. THIS RESULTED IN THE DISCHARGE OF AN UNKNOWN QUANTITY OF GASOLINE ONTO THE GROUND BEFORE THE EMERGENCY SHUTOFF WAS ACTIVATED. CALLER STATES THIS RESULTED IN THE POOLING OF GASOLINE ON THE ASPHALT THAT DAMAGED VEHICLES. CALLER STATES THIS WAS NEVER CLEANED UP, AND THE MATERIAL WENT DOWN A STORM DRAIN IN CLOSE PROXIMITY. CALLER STATES THE GAS STATION CREW DID NOT HAVE ANY TRAINING ON SPILL PROCEDURES/HAZARDOUS MATERIAL INCIDENTS, AND AS A RESULT NO RESPONSE ACTIONS WERE TAKEN. THE GAS STATION WAS EVACUATED DURING THE INCIDENT. CALLER STATES THE GAS STATION WAS IN THE PROCESS OF CHANGING OWNERSHIP DURING THIS INCIDENT.
